chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who hires another man for a house or a ship for a year, or more than that, or less. He said: 'The rent is binding upon him until the time for which he hired him, and the choice in taking the rent belongs to its owner; if he wishes, he takes it, and if he wishes, he leaves it.'
ai.seo_question: What are the rights and obligations regarding fixed-term rental contracts in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the binding nature of fixed-term lease agreements (*ijarah*), affirming that the tenant’s obligation to pay persists until the agreed term expires. It further establishes the landlord’s discretionary right (*khiyar*) to either collect the rent or forgive it, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of contractual stability balanced with the owner’s prerogative. This ruling underscores the importance of honoring temporal commitments in commercial transactions within Islamic law.
